_meta.purpose: Retry resolution for the 11 download failures from Task #3's first pass.
_meta.source_of_failures: Parsed from Posts/*/pdfs/download_log.json entries with status=failed.

failure_taxonomy.publisher_403: 6 entries - Wiley/BJSM/Taylor & Francis/MDPI blocked the direct publisher PDF URL even though Unpaywall flagged the paper as OA.
failure_taxonomy.pmc_html_fallback: 4 entries - backend-writer's downloader hit https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/<PMCID>/pdf/ (trailing slash, no filename) and got HTML instead of PDF. The new pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/<PMCID>/pdf/ endpoint is now fronted by a JavaScript proof-of-work challenge (cloudpmc-viewer-pow cookie, ~1.8KB HTML interstitial) that pure-urllib/requests clients cannot pass. This is a structural downloader blocker, not a URL bug.
failure_taxonomy.citation_doi_mismatch: 1 entry - Vieira 2024 Scand J Med Sci Sports 34(1):e14265. DOI 10.1111/sms.14265 is a COVID-in-athletes paper, NOT a training-to-failure paper. The post-side citation is either fabricated or wrong. No Vieira AF Scand J Med Sci Sports 2024 paper exists in PubMed at all. Frontend-writer must reconcile the citation before this can be resolved.

resolver_strategy: 1. For all PMC-hosted papers, use https://europepmc.org/articles/<PMCID>?pdf=render - confirmed to serve real application/pdf bytes for 5 of 7 PMCIDs tested from this host. No PoW gate.
2. For papers where EPMC returns HTTP 500 (observed on author-manuscript nihms*.pdf entries), mark unresolved_no_oa_mirror.
3. For papers with no PMC deposit at all, check EPMC for any fullTextUrlList[].documentStyle=='pdf' entry with availability='Open access'. If none, mark unresolved_not_oa.
4. Strict verification: every DOI/PMCID was confirmed via Unpaywall title match or NCBI DOI->PMCID converter. No fuzzy PubMed search was used here - that's Task #19's job on the original file.

5. Contact email for Unpaywall/NCBI calls: contentprinter@centralstrengthgyms.com. User-Agent used for verification HEAD checks was a generic browser UA because EPMC's ptpmcrender.fcgi endpoint closes connections on bot-UA (confirmed). Backend-writer should use the same generic UA to fetch these URLs.
backend_writer_instructions: Fetch every entry where status=='ok' and source.startswith('europepmc'). Set User-Agent to 'Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0 Safari/537.36' for these requests - the ContentPrinter/0.1 UA is blocked by EPMC's upstream service.
Validate response starts with b'%PDF-' before writing to disk - same guard as Task #3.
Write downloaded files to Posts/<slug>/pdfs/ref<NN>.pdf, overwriting any failed previous attempt.
Update Posts/<slug>/pdfs/download_log.json entries for these ref_idx values with the new url and status=ok.
For status=='unresolved_no_oa_mirror' and 'unresolved_not_oa' entries, leave the existing failed entry in place with an updated reason.
For status=='citation_doi_mismatch' (Vieira 2024), do NOT attempt download. Route to frontend-writer to fix the post.
frontend_writer_instructions: yt_training_past_failure ref01 (Vieira AF 2024) has a broken citation. The DOI given (10.1111/sms.14265) is a COVID-in-athletes paper, not training-to-failure. PubMed has NO Vieira AF paper in Scand J Med Sci Sports 2024 of any kind. Options: (a) drop the reference and renumber, (b) replace with a real training-to-failure paper - Grgic 2022 (ref02 in same post) and Martorelli 2017 (ref04) already cover that ground, or (c) find the original source the drafter was paraphrasing and cite it properly. This blocks the post from being published with credible references.
